sections.name: mock government adapter
sections.title: Mock adapter checks
sections.what: Checks the mock returns the same answer every time with the synthetic source and the not-official disclaimer, and that the bilingual workflow labels differ, the safe action list is fixed, and the Hindi caution uses the word for official.
sections.why: Confirms the demo answers stay clearly labelled and consistent across languages.
sections.watch_out: The Hindi check looks for one word, so it only proves that word is present.

summary: Checks that the mock government adapter returns stable, clearly labelled synthetic answers, and that the workflow wording means the same thing in English and Hindi.
purpose: Protects the labelling that stops demo answers being mistaken for official government status.
why: Likely reason: the app must never appear to speak for a government body, so the disclaimers and the synthetic flag are tested.
how: One test calls the mock twice and checks the result matches and carries the synthetic source and disclaimer. The other checks that the English and Hindi labels differ, that the safe actions are the expected list, and that the Hindi caution contains the word for official.
inputs: A demo case and a workflow stage name.
risks: The stage name is fixed in the test, so renaming the stage in the workflow file breaks it.
debug: If the disclaimer check fails, check the wording in the mock adapter. If the Hindi check fails, check the Hindi caution text in the workflow file.
